Amateur Radio Operator Certificate with Basic Qualification

note: Operator certification is governed by ISED; RBR-4 (formerly RIC-2, reclassified as RBR-4 in 2007; current Issue 3, July 2022) sets frequency privileges per qualification. A Basic Qualification alone is limited to bands above 30 MHz; all access below 30 MHz requires Basic with Honours (80%+ on the Basic exam) or the Advanced Qualification — a Basic holder with the 5 w.p.m. Morse Code qualification also has full HF access, though RBR-4 lists it as a separate qualification. RBR-4 does not grant Basic holders any sub-30 MHz segment; §11 only requires that signals automatically retransmitted below 29.5 MHz originate from an operator qualified below 30 MHz. Power caps: Basic — 560 W PEP (SSB), 190 W carrier (other emissions), or 250 W DC input; Advanced — 2250 W PEP (SSB), 750 W carrier, or 1000 W DC input; an external amplifier must not be capable of exceeding the applicable limit by more than 3 dB. Key deviations from the international table: 60m operation is channelized (five fixed channels, 2.8 kHz max bandwidth, 100 W PEP e.r.p., CW/data/phone emissions only, no interference protection, C21); 30m is a non-conforming Canadian allocation with no interference protection (C6); 40m 7200–7300 kHz must not constrain broadcasting (5.142); 219–220 MHz is secondary and 220–222 MHz only in exceptional circumstances such as disaster relief (C11). 2200m and 630m are capped at 1 W e.i.r.p. Authorized foreign amateurs receive Basic + Advanced privileges, capped by their home licence.
